scope: Conditional operator-reviewed exposure reduction and vendor update handoffs. Only Linux MPTCP has an opt-in executable host control. No universal hotfix.

profiles.name: Linux: temporarily stop creation of new MPTCP sockets
profiles.when_to_use: Only if a Linux system may be affected, the relevant vendor kernel fix is not active, and MPTCP disruption is acceptable.
before: Back up configuration and arrange service maintenance.
Identify all relevant network namespaces and MPTCP-using services.
Plan to restart affected MPTCP listeners; existing sockets may remain.
steps: Read the status without changing anything: python3 scripts/mptcp_guard.py status
If it reports available and enabled, inspect running services and approve the outage.
On the Linux host, run: sudo python3 scripts/mptcp_guard.py apply --accept-service-disruption
If services use separate network namespaces, have the administrator assess them individually. This helper manages only its current namespace.
Restart affected listeners during maintenance; inspect normal service traffic.
check: Run: python3 scripts/mptcp_guard.py status; expect knob value 0 in that namespace.
Confirm affected services remain functional without MPTCP; test ordinary IPv4 TCP connections.
Record date, namespace, running kernel and service status. Do NOT call the CVE fixed.
undo: After installing and rebooting into a vendor-fixed kernel, verify the exact running kernel vendor advisory.
If the original boot still has the guard state: sudo python3 scripts/mptcp_guard.py rollback --accept-reexposure
If reboot cleared the runtime guard, inspect current MPTCP setting and restore normal service configuration per vendor guidance.
Verify MPTCP-required applications, plus ordinary connections; close temporary exception ticket.
profiles.limitations: Only restricts creation of new MPTCP sockets in the current network namespace. Existing sockets, other namespaces and non-MPTCP attack paths remain outside its proof. Changes are runtime-only and lost on reboot. Applying and rolling back can interrupt services.

profiles.name: Windows: reduce exposure of an HTTP.sys HTTP/3 endpoint
profiles.when_to_use: Only for a vulnerable Windows HTTP.sys server exposing HTTP/3 that cannot yet take Microsoft's update. Requires server administrator.
before: Confirm HTTP.sys hosts HTTP/3; do not confuse browser HTTP/3 with the Windows HTTP.sys server.
Back up current HTTP.sys application and registry configuration. Arrange a maintenance window.
steps: Ask the server administrator to disable HTTP.sys HTTP/3 using their approved Microsoft-documented configuration, or restrict UDP/443 at the perimeter to trusted networks.
Do not assume a local Windows Firewall block works for every HTTP.sys QUIC listener.
Restart the affected service under the change plan; do not automatically restart the shared HTTP service.
check: From an authorized test client, confirm the service does not accept HTTP/3 on the restricted endpoint.
Confirm the normal HTTPS/TCP application path continues working and inspect service logs.
Record the effective network policy and HTTP.sys configuration; no CVE-fixed claim.
undo: Install Microsoft's signed update for the exact Windows edition and build, restart, verify active build and normal service function.
Restore the previous HTTP/3 policy/configuration in the approved maintenance window.
Test HTTP/3 and HTTPS/TCP with authorized clients.
profiles.limitations: Network rules can have exceptions or interception differences. Microsoft HTTP.sys is distinct from other QUIC stacks. This is administrator-assisted containment only.

profiles.name: Chrome: limit exposure until the official browser update is active
profiles.when_to_use: Google Chrome Stable cannot be updated promptly; do not assume the settings defeat the multi-bug exploit chain.
before: Do not open unknown sites or attachments in a known-affected browser.
Prefer pausing use of the affected browser until the vendor fix is installed.
steps: On a computer, open Chrome → Settings → Privacy and security → Security → Manage JavaScript optimization & security.
Select 'Don't allow sites to use JavaScript optimization' when available; the option may affect site performance or function.
For higher-risk systems, stop using the affected Chrome build until Google's signed update is available.
check: Reopen the settings page to confirm the setting is still selected.
Open a trusted page and check required actions; do not test an exploit.
undo: Use Chrome → Settings → About Chrome to install Google's signed stable update; relaunch.
Recheck the active full Chrome version and run the catalog version checker for each listed CVE.
Return settings to the site's approved baseline only after confirming the vendor update and acceptable risk.
profiles.limitations: V8 optimizer control is not established as a workaround for all Chrome chains or every CVE. It may not protect other vulnerabilities.

profiles.name: macOS Safari: restrict active web content pending Apple's fix
profiles.control: JavaScript permission and reduced untrusted browsing
profiles.when_to_use: A supported device cannot immediately install the Apple security update; not a universal Safari exploit block.
before: Prefer not to use the affected Safari build for untrusted websites until Apple's signed update is installed.
steps: On Mac, open Safari → Settings → Security.
Clear 'Enable JavaScript' if the organization accepts site breakage.
Avoid sensitive or unfamiliar browsing until the full vendor update is installed.
check: Reopen Safari Security settings and check JavaScript is still disabled.
Test a trusted page for acceptable basic function; many sites may fail.
undo: Install the relevant Apple OS/Safari security update using Software Update, then restart as instructed.
Confirm Safari/OS version against the exact Apple security advisory.
Re-enable JavaScript only under the approved local security policy and test sites.
profiles.limitations: Disabling JavaScript does not prove the WebKit exploit chain impossible; WebKit remains in use by other applications.

profiles.name: Android: avoid untrusted USB connection while waiting for verified device fix
profiles.when_to_use: Until an affected-device / fixed-build mapping is published for the lock-screen bypass.
before: Keep the device physically secured; a stolen device should be treated as exposed until its status is known.
steps: Do not connect a locked phone to an untrusted USB host, charging station or unknown accessory.
Use a personally controlled charger; keep operating system and Google Play system updates current.
Check the device manufacturer's security bulletin for exact model and build.
check: Open Settings → Security & privacy and Settings → System → Software updates (names vary by manufacturer).
Record the device model, Android security patch level and Google Play system update date.
If no vendor document maps this specific chain to a fixed build, mark its status UNKNOWN.
undo: Install the official device and Google updates when published for this exact model.
Verify the active software and security patch levels against the published advisory before closing the issue.
Keep device protection and physical security in place.
profiles.limitations: Physical precautions cannot retroactively protect a stolen device. No public CVE/fixed-build mapping is established for this chain here.

profiles.name: Nomad: restrict untrusted workload operations until edition-specific upgrade
profiles.control: operator-reviewed ACL and scheduler workload restrictions
profiles.when_to_use: Nomad Community 2.1.0 or earlier, or an affected Enterprise branch; only where operators cannot deploy the vendor fix immediately.
before: Identify every Nomad client and its edition/version; record whether clients run with elevated privileges.
Determine which identities can submit/dispatch/update jobs, and which jobs use exec/java drivers or sticky ephemeral disks.
Review business need and outage impact with cluster owner; capture current ACL policies and scheduler state.
steps: As an operator, restrict job submit/dispatch/update permissions to trusted service identities using existing Nomad ACL administration. Do not overwrite broad ACL policies automatically.
Review untrusted tenant use of exec/java task drivers and sticky ephemeral disks; temporarily suspend affected workloads only with owner approval.
Use vendor-signed packages to upgrade Community clients to 2.1.1+; Enterprise fixed lines are 2.1.0+ent, 1.11.12+ent and 1.10.18+ent. Coordinate servers/clients using supported upgrade guidance.
check: Confirm effective ACL restrictions and current running client version/edition on every affected node.
Perform authorized, non-exploit dispatch and same-client allocation replacement smoke tests; validate task files, ownership and workload health.
undo: After vendor fix verification and independent change review, restore approved submit/dispatch/update ACL permissions as needed.
Resume paused trusted workloads and confirm scheduling, logs, and migration behavior are healthy.
profiles.limitations: ACL restrictions and pausing workloads only reduce opportunity; they cannot prove avoidance of all symlink paths. Nomad Community 2.1.0 is not a fixed release. Upgrading Nomad requires coordinated vendor procedure and may not support downgrade.

profiles.name: Chrome MediaStream: update official Chrome Stable and limit untrusted browsing
profiles.control: urgent signed browser update / optional temporary browsing restriction
profiles.when_to_use: Official Chrome desktop Stable is below 156.0.8078.79 or an update is pending. Do not assume this version governs Android or forks.
before: Record the current full running version from chrome://settings/help and the browser distribution channel.
Save work and plan a browser relaunch.
steps: Use Chrome → Help → About Chrome to download Google’s signed Stable update, then relaunch.
If the update is unavailable, stop opening untrusted sites in the outdated browser; use an organization-approved updated browser if available.
check: Verify Chrome Stable is running at least 156.0.8078.79 on Windows/macOS/Linux and confirm vendor release applies.
Open a trusted test page and verify typical browser operations.
undo: Remove temporary browsing restrictions after running version, vendor applicability and normal function are confirmed.
Do not downgrade a patched Chrome browser to restore older behavior.
profiles.limitations: No local MediaStream binary fix or universal workaround; other Chromium-based browsers require their own advisories.

profiles.name: Delinea Windows Core Agent: restrict inbound TCP 5593 pending agent upgrade
profiles.control: Windows host firewall / GPO restriction of inbound agent TCP 5593
profiles.when_to_use: Affected Delinea Privilege Manager Windows Core Agents cannot be immediately updated. Obtain owner approval before changing remote policy-delivery behavior.
before: Inventory Windows Core Agent build and whether management is cloud or on premises.
Review the effective Windows Defender Firewall/GPO policy and identify application owners, management server IP addresses and required agent policy/revocation delivery deadlines.
Confirm remote access and a rollback path; use a pilot endpoint first.
steps: Cloud: configure centrally managed Windows inbound firewall policy to block TCP port 5593 for the affected agent, as described by Delinea.
On-premises: block inbound TCP 5593 or, if necessary, restrict source to the *verified* Privilege Manager web server IP; do not invent an IP, widen scope or use blanket firewall resets.
Validate and document changed agent pull/poll interval before rollout. Deploy the correct vendor-signed fixed Windows Core Agent build: 12.0.5804+ on the 12.x branch or 13.0.2064+ on the 13.x branch.
check: Inspect effective inbound firewall rules on the Windows endpoint and verify TCP 5593 is not accessible from unapproved networks.
Check policy update and privileged-access revocation timing under the new pull/poll behavior.
Verify the running Core Agent version and service health after vendor update.
undo: After confirmed vendor-fixed agent rollout, change review and policy-delivery validation, remove only the temporary named/managed firewall rule or revert that GPO change.
Recheck inbound exposure and that privilege policies still enforce correctly.
profiles.limitations: A firewall configuration is not the fixed agent; inbound TCP 5593 restriction can change delivery to scheduled polling on premises and affect urgent revocations. Only documented for Delinea Windows Core Agent; not a macOS/Linux fix.

profiles.name: ServiceNow AI Platform: confirm platform hotfix and restrict unneeded administrators
profiles.control: hosted service change record / role-access review (not host OS configuration)
profiles.when_to_use: A ServiceNow AI Platform instance has not been confirmed on a vendor-remediated branch/build.
before: Identify instance owner, hosted or self-hosted deployment, exact ServiceNow release, patch and hot fix build.
Record which identities need the admin role; assess effects of changes to workflow automations.
steps: For hosted instances obtain the ServiceNow maintenance/deployment confirmation. For partners/self-hosted obtain the applicable signed build or hotfix through ServiceNow Support (KB3228994).
Apply least-privilege review: revoke unnecessary admin role assignments only after approved access review; do not automatically remove roles or disable required automations.
Use the branch-specific vendor advisory; do not translate release names into numeric OS version floors.
check: Verify the active ServiceNow instance build and matching branch-specific vendor correction.
Test authorized administrative tasks, integrations and audit logs after role or release change.
undo: Restore only approved legitimate role assignments if access review found an operational issue.
Do not roll back an active security hotfix without ServiceNow support and risk approval.
profiles.limitations: This is a hosted/application issue, not an Ubuntu, Windows or macOS kernel hotfix. No stand-alone mitigation guarantees containment of a Rhino sandbox escape. Some branch fixes require authenticated vendor confirmation.

profiles.name: Veeam Management Pack: isolate management services and upgrade via supported 9a build
profiles.control: restrict service management-plane exposure and perform supported vendor upgrade
profiles.when_to_use: Veeam Management Pack for Microsoft System Center is on version 9.x or otherwise not confirmed at fixed build 13.1.0.334.
before: Identify affected Virtualization Extensions and Collector services, host and SCOM dependencies.
Back up configuration, capture service accounts, group memberships, approved management endpoints and upgrade documentation.
Confirm source Management Pack version 9a build 9.1.0.3107 before planning supported 13.1 upgrade; do not attempt an untested direct jump from older builds.
steps: Have the Windows/SCOM administrator limit unneeded network reachability to Veeam Management Pack management components using environment-specific least-access policy. Do not use invented universal ports or firewall IP ranges.
Review membership of Veeam Virtualization Extensions Users and domain accounts able to reach Collector; remove unnecessary grants only after access review.
Follow Veeam KB4949 supported upgrade path from 9a build 9.1.0.3107 to 13.1.0.334 with verified vendor packages and maintenance approval.
check: Confirm running Management Pack build 13.1.0.334 and service state for both Virtualization Extensions and Collector.
Validate SCOM collection, authorized remote management, scheduled jobs and audit logs.
undo: Restore only the specific temporary management-plane restrictions after documented vendor fix validation and change approval.
For upgrade problems follow Veeam-supported restore/recovery procedures; do not blindly downgrade or reinstall.
profiles.limitations: No universal Veeam binary hotfix or verified exploit-resistant firewall rule included. This advisory pertains to Veeam Management Pack, not Veeam Backup & Replication generally; source version and upgrade path matter.
